criterion_reviews.exact_text: Deliver bounded channel-specific CC123 commands with chronological ownership preflight, retained sustain/tails, zero-frame handling and unchanged saved configuration.
observed_coverage: All three variants pass channel_commands, command_partition, command_bounds and command_atomicity in the retained Linux integration and native host jobs; recovered macOS raw log lines 876-886, 894-898 and 906-910 confirm the corresponding selectors.

The independent map/multiset ownership oracle bypasses production NoteTracker translation/dispatch and invokes scalar engines over a 769-frame timeline plus 129-frame continuation at 32000/48000/96000/192000 Hz, float/double, whole/one-frame/fixed-64/ragged partitions. Required agreement is exact stereo sample bits, ownership/identities, mechanics, frame cursor and configuration.

Separate fixtures exercise 18 queues, 256 raw commands, 585 expanded physical-note actions, and 256 accepted versus 257 rejected actions per sample including sustain. Atomicity checks cover chronological reuse, shared-holder survival, late rejection, pending-recall abort/retry, inactive outputs and zero-frame nonadvancement.

Historical processor source copies and validates syntax before mailbox.begin_block, translates ownership on a candidate, aborts selected recall on preflight failure, and installs persistent state only after success. Channel commands sort by offset/channel, precede notes at ties, and render applies sustain before physical actions.

Ordinary CC123 releases preserve sustain, mechanics and filter tails; selected recall intentionally resets history. Legacy RHST-v1 bytes remain 16 bytes and exclude commands. The repaired loaded-MIDI restrike case was demonstrated sensitive to wrong ordering in W3-048 and passes all three native platforms.

Generic release-port fault injection does not execute the combined host-publication failure. Accepted arithmetic failures retain partial accepted state and require reset; they are not preflight rollback.
Finite synthetic fixtures and fixed storage do not prove arbitrary foreign getters, native DAW delivery or a worst-case device deadline.
